pr_body:
- Today when we make endpoints for the ModelDataSource, we apply the callbacks to the EndpointBuilder before creating the endpoint. This happens every time anyone accesses the endpoints property. Instead of re-applying the conventions, we do it once on Build. We also throw if more conventions are added after building.
- Added tests

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/34199

issue_context.title: RouteEndpoint metadata from convention builders are duplicated
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

When inspecting endpoints with `EndpointDataSource`, for example in an `IApiDescriptionProvider`, some of the metadata on `RouteEndpoint` instances is duplicated. As shown in the screenshot below, there are two duplicated HTTP method metadata items.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1439341/124929716-a0f18b80-dff8-11eb-8144-47d1c6874c74.png)

Tracing through the code, this appears to be caused by a number of factors that together contribute to the routing endpoint conventions for an endpoint builder being run multiple times. The screenshot below shows the HTTP method metadata being added to the endpoint builder a second time.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1439341/124929684-9cc56e00-dff8-11eb-9ba7-80c9a8314975.png)

The contributing factors to this issue appear to be:

1. There are two `CompositeEndpointDataSource` instances created by the application: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/5577c0d128fd30d800f434e6a629978916f7d64e/src/Http/Routing/src/EndpointRoutingMiddleware.cs#L44 https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/5577c0d128fd30d800f434e6a629978916f7d64e/src/Http/Routing/src/DependencyInjection/RoutingServiceCollectionExtensions.cs#L65
2. Each `CompositeEndpointDataSource` enumerates the `Endpoints` property of each underlying endpoint data source once: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/5577c0d128fd30d800f434e6a629978916f7d64e/src/Http/Routing/src/CompositeEndpointDataSource.cs#L115
3. `ModelEndpointDataSource` calls `Build()` on each convention builder each time the `Endpoints` property is accessed https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/5577c0d128fd30d800f434e6a629978916f7d64e/src/Http/Routing/src/ModelEndpointDataSource.cs#L35
4. Each call to `Build()` runs the convention action(s): https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/5577c0d128fd30d800f434e6a629978916f7d64e/src/Http/Routing/src/DefaultEndpointConventionBuilder.cs#L30-L33
5. The conventions may mutate the endpoint builder's state multiple times: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/5577c0d128fd30d800f434e6a629978916f7d64e/src/Http/Routing/src/Builder/RoutingEndpointConventionBuilderExtensions.cs#L111-L117

The net result is that every time the `Endpoints` property of an `ModelEndpointDataSource` is accessed, the number of `Metadata` items on a route endpoint increases by the number of conventions configured.

Below is an example of four duplicate metadata items in a sample application:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1439341/124933540-e1063d80-dffb-11eb-8869-13b110ac552c.png)

### To Reproduce

To reproduce this issue, edit [this test](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/5577c0d128fd30d800f434e6a629978916f7d64e/src/Mvc/test/WebSites/SimpleWebSiteWithWebApplicationBuilder/Program.cs#L11) to have the following code:

```csharp
app.MapGet("/json", (IApiDescriptionGroupCollectionProvider provider) =>
{
    if (provider.ApiDescriptionGroups is not null)
    {
        // Used to inspect and debug ApiDescriptionGroups
    }

    return Json(new Person("John", 42));
});
```

Then debug the [`JsonResult_Works()`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/b9efadc59ddbf6743775244622fb95301dd1846c/src/Mvc/test/Mvc.FunctionalTests/SimpleWithWebApplicationBuilderTests.cs#L34) test with a breakpoint set here:

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/b9efadc59ddbf6743775244622fb95301dd1846c/src/Mvc/Mvc.ApiExplorer/src/EndpointMetadataApiDescriptionProvider.cs#L59

Inspecting `routeEndpoint.Metadata` with the debugger will show the duplicated metadata as shown in the preceding screenshots.

### Further technical details

- ASP.NET Core version `6.0.0-preview.7.21357.1`
- .NET Core SDK `6.0.100-preview.7.21357.57`
- Visual Studio 2022 17.0.0 Preview 1.1
comments:
Thanks for contacting us.
We're moving this issue to the `Next sprint planning` milestone for future evaluation / consideration. Because it's not immediately obvious that this is a bug in our framework, we would like to keep this around to collect more feedback, which can later help us determine the impact of it. We will re-evaluate this issue, during our next planning meeting(s). 
If we later determine, that the issue has no community involvement, or it's very rare and low-impact issue, we will close it - so that the team can focus on more important and high impact issues.
To learn more about what to expect next and how this issue will be handled you can read more about our triage process [here](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/master/docs/TriageProcess.md).

review_comments: It's interlocked because we're worried about `Add` / `Build` being called concurrently?
I'm just being extra defensive. It's unclear if these APIs are intended to be called thread safe. This is just to prevent any corruption.
